sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (true/false, match the columns, fill in the blanks or give reasons).

questions.q: State True or False. (i) At 16 years Rahul will get hair on his face. (ii) Priya will gain 2 cm height at the age of 12. (iii) Nocturnal emission is normal for boys. (iv) Most girls and boys suffer from acne during adolescence.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) False: girls gain about 8 cm in the year. (iii) True. (iv) True.

questions.q: Give reasons for the following behaviour of adolescents: (i) worry about their looks (ii) peculiar talking and dressing (iii) intense love towards a much older person of the opposite sex (iv) feel parents do not understand them.
questions.answer: (i) Rapid body changes make them feel 'on stage'. (ii) They follow the peer group culture. (iii) It is a 'crush', a typical stage. (iv) Rebellion and the generation gap.

questions.q: Identify two characteristics of language development of adolescents. (a) Using fluent and complex language (b) Liking tongue twisters (c) Using similar words with different meanings (d) Liking slang.
Match Column A with Column B. A: (a) Early maturing boys (b) Late maturing boys. B: (i) Feel inferior (ii) Confident and chosen as leaders (iii) Look young and are relaxed.
Fill in the blanks. (a) The WHO defines adolescents as persons aged ________ years. (b) The legal age of marriage for boys is ________ years.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Explain why adolescents need proper sex education and what role parents can play.
questions.answer: Adolescents become sexually mature and peers and printed matter give wrong information. Parents should build an open relationship and give correct answers to their questions.

or.q: Describe the typical characteristics of adolescent thinking that distinguish it from childhood thinking.
or.answer: Adolescents think abstractly and can imagine and think contrary to fact ideas. They consider all alternatives and understand similes and abstract jokes, unlike children who need to see things.

questions.q: Explain the effects of early maturation in adolescent boys and girls.
questions.answer: Early maturing boys are confident and chosen as leaders but adults expect more from them. Early maturing girls feel conscious and odd and are expected to behave like adults.

questions.q: Why is peer group important to adolescents? Give two reasons.
questions.answer: Everybody has the same conflicts and peers seem more understanding than parents. It lets them learn to interact with the opposite sex and follow peer culture.

questions.q: List two harmful effects of peer pressure.
questions.answer: Adolescents may be pressurised to try drugs, alcohol or smoking. They may shoplift or act against their own judgement and later regret it.

questions.q: Mention two problems of adolescents.
questions.answer: Eating disorders such as undereating or overeating and suicidal tendencies from loneliness. Peer pressure and teenage pregnancy are also problems.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the effect of early and late maturation on adolescents (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Early maturing girls feel conscious and odd, while late maturing girls are relaxed but ignored by boys. (ii) Early maturing boys are confident leaders. (iii) Late maturing boys feel inferior; these feelings are temporary and parents should explain the changes.

questions.q: Discuss the various ways in which parents discipline adolescents (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Giving freedom with interest develops independence and responsibility. (ii) Strict, authoritative control hampers independence. (iii) Indifference gives indifferent children, so respect and love are best.

questions.q: Explain the role of the school in adolescence (three points).
questions.answer: (i) A school that is not harsh and respects students' views makes them enjoy studies. (ii) Warm trained teachers recognise talents and motivate; poor teachers lead to drop-outs. (iii) Teachers can bridge the generation gap.

questions.q: Enumerate three developmental tasks of adolescence.
questions.answer: (i) Accepting one's physique and using it effectively. (ii) Achieving emotional independence from parents. (iii) Achieving a set of values and preparing for a career and family life.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the physical, social and cognitive changes of adolescence, and the problems adolescents face.
questions.answer: (i) Boys grow muscles, broad shoulders, facial hair and their voice breaks; girls get rounded contours, broad hips and menarche. (ii) Girls mature about two years earlier than boys. (iii) Socially they prefer the peer group and its culture. (iv) Thinking becomes abstract and systematic. (v) Typical features are preoccupation with looks, crushes, idealism, rebellion and mood swings. (vi) Problems include eating disorders, suicidal tendencies, peer pressure, biological problems and teenage pregnancy.
